The site classification systems for soils are used to categorise the geological and geotechnical properties of a site in order to assess its response to seismic activity. The site soil shall be classified in accordance with SCE/SEI 7-22 [-@ASCE722] based on the average shear wave velocity parameter, $\bar v_S$, which is derived from the measured shear wave velocity profile from the ground surface to a depth of 30 m. The average shear wave velocity $\bar v_S$ is used to characterize the foundation and account for seismic site conditions. N-values from Standard Penetration Test (SPT) ^[Numerous correlations have been developed between SPT N values and $\bar v_S$ and are summarised in a report by the @PEER2012] or Cone Penetration Test (CPT) can be used to estimate shear wave velocities of the foundation materials. Profiles containing distinct soil and rock layers shall be subdivided into those layers designated by a number that ranges from $1$ to $n$ at the bottom, where there is a total of $n$ distinct layers in the 30 m. The symbol $i$ refers to any one of the layers between $1$ and $n$. The average shear wave velocity, $\bar v_S$, shall be determined according to the following formula:

$$\bar v_S = \frac{30 \ m} {\sum_{j=1}^{n} \frac {d_j} {v_{S_j}}}$$

where $d_i,d_j$ is the thickness of any layer between 0 and 30 m, ${v_{S_j}}$ is the shear-wave velocity in $m/s$ and $\sum_{i=1}^{n} d_i=30 \ m$ is the profile depth.
